messages.subject: Group level SCN - Permutation
messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon,

I just had a couple of questions about permutations for the group-level SCN. For the bootstrap function, an arbitrary amount of groups can be used and the function provides CIs for each of the groups. This works fine for me as I have three groups being compared.

However, my experience is that the permutation function does not work for arbitrary numbers of groups (instead just reports a comparison between the first two groups listed). Is there a way in which I can do permutations between groups (without having to recalculate residuals etc for only the two groups being compared?)

I would test myself but due to the long time it takes to run the permute function on my local machine it isn't the easiest to troubleshoot!
My current commands are as follows:

myPerms <- permute::shuffleSet(n=nrow(all.dat.resids$resids.all), nset=kNumPerms)
perms.all <- brainGraph_permute(densities, all.dat.resids, perms=myPerms, N=kNumPerms, level='graph', atlas=atlas, auc=TRUE)

If I run:

myPerms <- permute::shuffleSet(n=nrow(all.dat.resids$resids.all[all.dat.resids$resids.all=='Group1'|'Group2'), nset=kNumPerms)
perms.all <- brainGraph_permute(densities, all.dat.resids, perms=myPerms, N=kNumPerms, level='graph', atlas=atlas, auc=TRUE)

would that suffice?

BW
Dan

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Group level SCN - Permutation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dan, as far as I know, that is just how permutation-based inference works;
i.e., it results in a single metric. This is most often (I would think) a
difference in group means (or medians), or something similar. But I don't know
of a way to calculate the pairwise differences between 3 groups without doing
all of the calculations.

Chris

P.S. If you want to troubleshoot, you can always set the number of permutations
to a very low number.

P.P.S. If "resids.all" is a data.table (which it should be), you can simplify
your command as
all.dat.resids$resids.all[Group %in% c('Group1', 'Group2'), .N]

I thought that might be the case. Previously, I  had just subsetted the residuals to groups A and B calculate, then subset to B and C and compare and then A and C. However, because the brainGraph_permute function requires the all.dat.resids object, I'm not sure it is as easy to subset as it was for when it just needed the resids.all data table (which was subset-able).

BW
Dan

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Group level SCN - Permutation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dan, actually I wrote an S3 method for that purpose. If "all.dat.resids" is
the output of your "get.resid" call, then you can directly subset by group. I
don't remember if I had tried doing it for more than 1 group at a time, but you
should be able to use the "[" operator, such as:

residsAB <- all.dat.resids[c('GroupA', 'GroupB')]

Please try that out and let me know if it works.

Chris

messages.subject: Update to v2.7.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello, a couple days ago I updated the package to v2.7.0. For the full change set, please see NEWS.md at the github repo.

The big changes are:

`brainGraph_init` has been replaced by `import_scn` (where "scn" means "structural connectivity networks". The most useful feature here is that it is no longer necessary to abbreviate the region names in the Freesurfer output files; the code to do that was formerly in Chapter 3 of the User Guide. So, now you can simply point to the outputs from "aparcstats2table" and "asegstats2table". Please read Chapters 3 and 6 of the User Guide for any details.
The output from `aop` and `loo` are now an S3 class (the class name is "IC"). There is a new `summary` and `plot` method. The `plot` method replaces the code chunks that were in Chapter 14 of the User Guide; so now, you simply have to type, for example:
plot(RC.loo)

I plan on making more updates (mostly related to improving interactive exploration and extraction of useful information from analysis results) over the next several weeks.

Please let me know if there are any issues.
Chris
